chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darraj, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, who said:
I saw Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) spread the soil upon the deceased, so he held it for a while in his hand, then spread it, and he did not exceed three handfuls.

He said, so I asked him about that, and he said: O Umar! I was saying: 'Belief in You and confirmation of Your Resurrection. This is what Allah and His Messenger promised,' up to His words, 'submission'.
Thus was what the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) used to do, and by it the Sunnah has flowed.
ai.seo_question: What is the prescribed number of handfuls of soil to spread on the deceased during burial according to Shia tradition?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi details the specific Sunnah of the Prophet and Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) in burial rites, where soil is spread in three handfuls while reciting verses affirming faith in resurrection and submission. This practice underscores the Shia emphasis on emulating the Prophet’s physical actions as a tangible expression of theological belief in the Hereafter. The act serves as a practical demonstration of trust in the divine promise, linking ritual precision with spiritual conviction.
